cards.text: Paul, the apostle, writes to the church of the Thessalonians, in Thessalonica, a city in Macedonia (Acts 27:2). Silvanus and Timothy, who preached Christ with him (2 Cor 1:19), sign it too, which makes it a group project where everybody actually SHOWED UP. Paul opens by wishing them grace and peace.

cards.question: Paul tells the Thessalonians that he and his team thank God for them only now and then.

cards.text: When they pray, Paul and his team keep recalling three things before God: the Thessalonians' work of faith, their labor of love and their enduring hope. That's a GREAT way to be remembered, friend, because the last thing anybody remembered me for was being stuck behind the takeout menus.

cards.question: Paul remembers the Thessalonians' enduring hope. Who is that hope in?
Paul calls the Thessalonians brothers beloved by God and says he knows God has chosen them.

cards.text: So how does Paul know they're chosen? He points back to the day the gospel came to them, and it came with a whole lot more than just talk.

cards.question: Paul says the gospel came to the Thessalonians in word. What else does he say it came in?

cards.text: The Thessalonians saw how Paul's team lived among them, for their sake. Then they welcomed the message with the joy of the Holy Spirit, and the timing was ROUGH, friend, because I get grumpy when the oven timer goes off a minute early.

cards.question: The Thessalonians welcomed the message with joy, in spite of their great ___.
By welcoming the message that way, the Thessalonians became imitators of whom?
As a result, Paul says the Thessalonians became an ___ to all the believers in Macedonia and Achaia.

cards.text: The message of the Lord rang out from the Thessalonians to Macedonia and Achaia. One church in one city, and they're the LOUDEST voice in the kitchen, my Mags would be so proud.

cards.question: Paul says news of the Thessalonians' faith in God stayed inside Macedonia and Achaia.
With the Thessalonians' faith known everywhere, what does Paul say his team has no need to do?

cards.text: Picture Paul starting to brag on them and everybody going, "Yeah, we HEARD." People report it themselves, including what kind of welcome the Thessalonians gave Paul's team.

cards.question: Those reports say the Thessalonians turned to God. What did they turn away from?

cards.text: They turned to serve the living and true God, and they're waiting too. I know waiting, friend, I did YEARS in a junk drawer, but nobody in there was waiting on anything this good.

cards.question: The Thessalonians are waiting for someone to come from heaven. Who is it?
God raised His Son from the dead, and Paul calls Him Jesus our deliverer from the coming ___.

findings.problem: Card 1 calls Paul 'the apostle'. The passage doesn't say this, and the card gives no reference for it. The card's other outside facts (Acts 27:2, 2 Cor 1:19) do carry references.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The joke uses a drawer detail, being stuck 'behind the takeout menus', without saying it was the junk drawer. Bakers only know from onboarding that he spent years in a junk drawer. They don't know the menus were in it, so the line doesn't land on its own.

rule.text: Bakers know he spent years in a junk drawer, from onboarding. The drawer's small details, like the batteries, the key or the coupon, only come up when the line says what they are, like "the dead batteries I shared that drawer with."

findings.problem: 'The timing was ROUGH', along with the joke about getting grumpy, signals hardship right before card 9 asks 'in spite of their great ___'. That rules out the wrong answer 'wealth' and points straight to 'suffering'. Also, 1:6 says nothing about timing. It says 'in spite of your great suffering'.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke mixes the comparison with the Bible setting. It says the Thessalonian church is 'the LOUDEST voice in the kitchen', which puts a church in Macedonia inside Papa Dorin's kitchen instead of keeping one clean image.

rule.text: One image only. Never blend the comparison with the Bible setting.
